label: Peace treaty with the Hittites recorded
more: In Ramesses II's Year 21 (about 1259 BC, Shaw) Egypt and the Hittite king Hattusili III agreed not to attack each other and to help each other against a third power. The Egyptian text is carved on the Cachette Court wall and at the Ramesseum; Hittite tablets were found at Hattusa.

label: Temple of Khonsu begun
more: Ramesses III (reigned 1184 to 1153 BC) began the temple of the moon god Khonsu, reusing older blocks. The exact year is unknown, so 1170 is only a mid-reign marker. Ramesses XI and Herihor built the front, and Taharqa and the Ptolemies added to it.

label: Cachette of statues found (to 1905)
more: In December 1903 Georges Legrain began finding hundreds of statues buried in a water-filled pit in the Cachette Court, probably in Greek times. His team lifted the water out by shaduf. The IFAO's study dates the work to four seasons ending in July 1907.
